briefs: Create a luminous architectural print: saturated colour fields, careful structural linework, real curves and unusually attentive window/cornice detail. Keep the image alive rather than diagrammatic.

Create a richly observed coloured engraving: dense but selective architectural line, subtle hatching, deep warm/cool colour, and strong spatial depth. Do not reduce the facade to repeated rectangular holes.

Create an opaque, tactile architectural painting: visible dry brush decisions, warm/cool colour relationships, convincing geometry and very specific architectural accents. Avoid a generic oil-paint filter.

Create an inventive cut-paper/overprint city portrait: layering and registration slips, curved and faceted forms, strong colour atmosphere, and precision where the building is distinctive. Not a flat icon.

Create a cinematic street portrait in coloured ink: deliberate light and shadow, layered facade depth and detailed joinery; fewer marks in secondary areas. Keep the recognisable building, not an imagined replacement.

Choose your own distinctive visual language for this photograph, using the instrument freely. Prioritise architectural richness and immersive colour over decorative texture. Make an interpretation worth exploring, not just a technically correct sketch.
